messages:
Nora (CS): Glyph reported higher p99 and some stream stalls after their feature flip. Renewal touchpoint next week, want a concise ops 'cheatsheet' they can run through with their infra folks. Can we draft one here?
Lee (Eng): Sure. Keep it checklist-style: quick mitigations + why it helps + one command/snippet.
Priya (Onboarding): They asked for something they can paste into their runbook and share in DevOps channels. Short bullets only.
Lee (Eng): Proposed sections: 1) Confirm priming headers, 2) Enable tenant hot-prefix cache, 3) Client-side bundling, 4) Streaming chunk tuning, 5) Fallback model header.
Nora (CS): For each item add expected impact like "reduces tail ~30%" or "cuts request QPS by ~3x".
Lee (Eng): Draft bullets: 
- Priming header: Add header X-Client-Priming: true on initial warmup requests. Why: routes to warm pools. Impact: lowers cold-start tail.
- Hot-prefix cache: Tenant scope, TTL 20s. Command: curl -H 'X-Tenant: glyph' -X POST /prefill. Impact: repeated prompts p50/p95 down.
- Bundling: Bundle up to 6 logical requests, max delay 30ms. Snippet: // pseudo client.batchSend({maxBatch:6,maxWaitMs:30}) Impact: reduces per-request overhead and smoothing.
- Stream tuning: Use chunk_tokens=64 to avoid head-of-line blocking. Toggle fallback: X-Disable-Streaming: true. Impact: smoother end-to-end UX when downstream is flaky.
- Fallback model: Header X-Model-Fallback: compact-1 for degraded capacity. Impact: keeps service available with slightly lower throughput cost.
Priya (Onboarding): Add quick telemetry checks: warm-pool hit rate, prefill latency, per-route p99, bundle success rate. Also a tiny feedback template: 3 yes/no + 1 freeform.
Nora (CS): Nice. Include two troubleshooting steps: 
- If tail spikes after deploy: verify cache warm-up, increase TTL to 30s, enable async prefill.
- If error surge on origin: add token-bucket throttle on prefill fetches and revert bundling to smaller batch size.
ops-bot: Note: created doc "glyph-ops-cheatsheet-v1" at /shared/cs-assets.
Priya (Onboarding): I'll convert to a one-pager and wire in a tiny JS snippet and curl examples. Will keep language non-prescriptive.
Lee (Eng): I'll add the safe default values in a separate code block for their engineers. Example JSON: {"cache_scope":"tenant","cache_ttl":20,"bundle_max":6,"bundle_delay_ms":30,"stream_chunk_tokens":64}
Nora (CS): Action items: @Priya produce the one-pager (EOD), @Lee add the safe defaults and troubleshooting (EOD). I'll schedule a 20-min runbook review with Glyph tomorrow.
Priya (Onboarding): Ack. Will post draft link here when ready.
Nora (CS): Thanks team 44d.
note: Short Slack thread drafted for a customer-facing cheatsheet; formatted as a single continuous string per agents.md guidelines.
